---
title: "First seen and last seen"
description: "How OPDI defines the first and last report of a track (first_seen and last_seen events and columns) and the track duration."
---

## In one sentence

`first_seen` and `last_seen` are the first and last time the aircraft of a
track was really heard, as events and as columns of the flight list.

## What it needs

The cleaned reports of the track (see
[Cleaning of position reports](cleaning.qmd)).

## How it is computed

1. Take the reports of the track with a **measured position**: one that the
   cleaning did not empty. OpenSky keeps sending an aircraft's last state for
   about 300 s after it was last heard; cleaning empties these repeated values,
   so the last measured position is the last time the aircraft was heard.
2. `first_seen` is the first of these reports and `last_seen` the last.
3. A track with no measured position at all uses its first and last report
   with any measured value (altitude, speed, heading or vertical rate); a
   track with none of these uses its first and last report.
4. Each event takes the position, altitude and measurements of its report.
5. `track_duration_min` is `last_seen` minus `first_seen`, in minutes.

The same definition is used in the flight list and in the events, so the two
always agree. Every track has one `first_seen` and one `last_seen` event.

## Based on

Developed for OPDI.

## What is published

Event types `first_seen` and `last_seen`, with position, altitude,
`distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`; their `info` is empty. Flight list
columns `first_seen`, `last_seen` and `track_duration_min`.

## Use cases

- **Where reception starts and ends**: maps of `first_seen` and `last_seen`
  positions show where the receivers lose aircraft.
- **Filter fragments**: a very short `track_duration_min` is often a piece of
  a flight on the ground; choose your own limit.
- **Time passed**: every event's `time_passed_s` counts from `first_seen` (see
  [Time passed](time-passed.qmd)).

## Limitations

They describe reception, not the flight: an aircraft is first seen where a
receiver first hears it, at the stand, on the runway or in the air. See
[Limitations: first and last seen](../limitations.qmd#lim-first-last-seen).

## Availability and accuracy

Every track has both. They are not compared with a reference, because no
record gives when a receiver heard an aircraft.
